analysis.narrative_assessment: The current titles name topics (Product, Traction, Team) rather than takeaways, so the story depends on the presenter. The recommended headlines carry the problem, product, early demand, forecast, and ask as one argument, while flagging the pilot-count conflict and the unevidenced team.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Tidewater Analytics helps municipal water utilities find leaks with clip-on acoustic sensors.
slide_reviews.key_fact: Acoustic leak detection for municipal water utilities
slide_reviews.significance: Names the customer and the problem solved on the first slide
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Acoustic leak detection for municipal water utilities

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Utilities lose an estimated 6 billion gallons of treated water daily, and most leaks surface only after damage.
slide_reviews.key_fact: Estimated 6 billion gallons/day lost; leaks found after surface damage
slide_reviews.significance: Frames a large, costly problem for utilities
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: US utilities lose an estimated 6 billion gallons of treated water per day (industry estimate cited by the company)
slide_reviews.evidence_gap: The underlying industry source is not named on the slide.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Clip-on hydrant sensors and a leak-detection model give repair crews a ranked leak list each morning.
slide_reviews.key_fact: Clip-on acoustic sensors on hydrants plus a machine-learning model
slide_reviews.significance: Crews start each day knowing which leaks to fix first
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Repair crews receive a ranked leak list each morning

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: A completed Marlow pilot and a signed Harbor County contract show early utility demand.
slide_reviews.key_fact: One completed pilot, one signed contract ($180K ACV), two letters of intent
slide_reviews.significance: Early validation from paying and piloting utilities
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Harbor County | Signed contract | $180K annual contract value
slide_reviews.evidence_gap: Clarify which pilot leak count is correct.
slide_reviews.conflict_note: Slide 4 reports 14 leaks located in 90 days; slide 11 reports 12 leaks confirmed by excavation in 90 days.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Per-sensor annual subscriptions of $1,200 are designed to create recurring utility revenue.
slide_reviews.key_fact: $1,200 per sensor per year plus $150 one-time installation
slide_reviews.significance: Recurring revenue that scales with sensors deployed
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Annual subscription: $1,200 per sensor per year
slide_reviews.evidence_gap: No renewal or retention data yet shows the revenue is recurring in practice.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Management forecasts revenue rising from a projected $0.4M in 2026 to $5.2M in FY2028.
slide_reviews.significance: Shows the growth plan investors are underwriting
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Forecast: $5.2M revenue in FY2028 (projected, not actual)
slide_reviews.evidence_gap: Assumptions behind the forecast are not shown.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: A leak alerts dashboard ranks hydrant, main, and valve alerts by severity for each zone.
slide_reviews.key_fact: Dashboard listing zone alerts with high/medium/low severity
slide_reviews.significance: Shows crews what to inspect first
slide_reviews.evidence_excerpt: Image shows a 'Leak alerts dashboard' listing Zone 4 hydrant 112 as high severity
slide_reviews.evidence_gap: Slide has no title or extractable text.

slide_reviews.recommended_headline: Dana Ruiz leads as CEO and Sam Okafor as CTO; relevant experience is not yet shown.

main_deck_narrative.headline: Tidewater Analytics helps municipal water utilities find leaks with clip-on acoustic sensors.

Per-sensor annual subscriptions of $1,200 are designed to create recurring utility revenue.
Management forecasts revenue rising from a projected $0.4M in 2026 to $5.2M in FY2028.
A leak alerts dashboard ranks hydrant, main, and valve alerts by severity for each zone.
Dana Ruiz leads as CEO and Sam Okafor as CTO; relevant experience is not yet shown.
